g.text: Did you have family growing up?
Do you mean, did I have parents?
No, I came from a test tube.
I meant more like siblings. Cousins. Etc.
Oh. Not technically? But all us kids on the Zariman were basically raised together.
There's a reason I don't like the Man in the Wall.
I don't want to talk about it.
It... It wasn't pretty. Why're you asking?
Eleanor. She's driving me up the wall and I didn't know how much you'd understand.
You know she and I are a "thing," right?
She drives me nuts for a completely *different* reason. ;)
I'm not looking for gossip, mate. Or to start any nonsense.
It's more about what she's not doing.
AUGH. No. No, no, no! She's my SISTER!
I'm just worried about her, is all.
There's an anniversary that we've...celebrated is the wrong word.
She can invade my mind any time...
And she missed it this year. She never does.
IN ALL THE NAMES OF SOL, STOP.
This has been a... pretty messed up year, to be fair. Maybe she just forgot?
Can I ask what you were supposed to be commiserating?
Have you just asked her about it?
*Sigh.* You have a sick sense of humour, mate.
It's not really my story to tell, it's hers.
I was left on my own too much.
We lost someone who was important to both of us.
Then why're you bothering me? Go ask *her* what's up.
Anyway. About Eleanor? Whats she doing?
Have you talked to her about missing the date?
Right. Well, now that I've managed to scrub my brain down with bleach, it's more about what she's not doing.
No. And I honestly couldn't tell you why. Instead, I'm here talking to you.
I assume whatever this event that you're commiserating was painful.
Maybe now that everything in your lives have changed, you want to let it go? Maybe she does, too?
Maybe. Maybe it is time to move on from the past. Which is ironic, considering your situation.
Eh, there's a difference between choosing to stay and being trapped. Trust me.
I like the view, what can I say?
Heh. Well. Thanks, all the same.
You going to tell me what all this was about?
I will. Just... when I've had some time to think.
